name: North Face
text: [overview] best in winter or spring, when the two main approaches are easier with snow cover.
[overview] The first goes up steep snow to a 30 ft rock band, then more snow with boulders suitable for sling anchors.
[overview] With the band snowed over it felt about 5.7 / M2+, and good gear turned up after digging.
[overview] The second is 55-degree snow up to the boulder on top (5.4, easier on the back side).
[detailed_rack] A picket or two is optional.

name: Mt. Michelson, South Face
text: [overview] The southern side departs from the glacier of that name, covers 1000-2000' of loose blocks, talus and snow, and then follows a final line of snow and ice up to the crest of the summit ridge.
[detailed_rack] A few pickets and ice screws may help.

name: Col of the Wild
text: [overview] brief cruxes of ice or mixed rock appear now and then, with much simulclimbing on steep snow.
[overview] Near the top a large cornice may need tunneling.
[detailed_rack] Standard alpine rack: some small and medium cams, a nut selection, knifeblades, angles, screws for ice, specters and a few pickets.

name: Kissing up the choss pile
text: [approach] From the Reed Lakes lot, walk to the former building site, short of Nugget Boulder and the Snowbird slab.
[approach] Then take the path bearing left up the drainage, past the Snowbird mine on your right, and keep going up the bowls to the pass.
[approach] The Snowbird Glacier lies below the pass, and the Nunatak is the small formation beside it.

name: The Friends Along the Way
text: [overview] A couloir with over 2500 feet of gain, with snow close to vertical and traverses over chossy rock sections.
[overview] The first fork: steep snow if you go right, then 50 feet of steep choss;
[overview] going left means far steeper snow and some snow bridges.
[detailed_rack] A rope and a skeleton rack are worth carrying if snow anchors for descending are within your skills.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — required

name: Smoke em' if you got em'
text: [overview] Pitches 1-3 are the couloir (simul-climbing is possible depending on snow quality);
[detailed_rack] 3-6 snow pickets, cams from .5 to #2, and a full set of nuts.

name: Splitter Choss
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — optional for the approach

name: North Gully
text: [overview] Turning right gives the main gully, snow with WI2 steps to the top;
[overview] Descent options: by way of Thunder-East Glacier, steep creek, or downclimbing or rappelling the gully.
[detailed_rack] Ice screws, and perhaps a picket or two.

name: West Ridge
text: [detailed_rack] Cams to #2 BD, 1-2 ice screws, plus crampons, an ice axe and glacier equipment.

name: West Ridge
text: [descent_text] From the summit, put on crampons and descend west on snow or ice until the scree slopes leading toward Twincicle Pass appear.
[descent_text] Go down through Twincicle Pass and the Twincicle Valley, which is a tangle of alders, and cross the short but very steep Twincicle Glacier.

name: West Twincil
text: [overview] alternatively stop above and climb a near-vertical snow step 10-20 ft tall to a ledge, from which a wider couloir continues to the basin below.
[detailed_rack] Steep snow and complex avalanche terrain;
[detailed_rack] consult snow and avalanche forecasts beforehand.
[approach] The line is steep, narrow and avalanche-prone, so it is best entered in very stable conditions after studying the map and the snow.
